document.title: Office 365 → Google Workspace Migration & Active Directory Unjoining

customer.profile: Miles Partnership is a creative marketing agency operating primarily on Google Workspace, with Microsoft 365 retained for mail and calendar. The majority of file content is already on Google Drive; mailboxes, OneDrive, SharePoint, and approximately 225 domain-joined endpoints remain on Microsoft infrastructure.

stakeholders.name: David Laffitte
stakeholders.title: IT Lead
stakeholders.description: Day-to-day technical lead, user mapping and decision owner

background.objective:
Miles Partnership, a creative marketing agency with approximately 444 active users, is partnering with Premier Cloud Inc., a Google Cloud Premier Partner, to migrate from Microsoft 365 to Google Workspace and decommission its on-premises Active Directory (AD) infrastructure.

The objective of this engagement is to execute an end-to-end migration of mail (approximately 8.1 TB across 768 mailboxes), files (14.7 TB OneDrive and 2.0 TB SharePoint), and endpoint identity (approximately 225 domain-joined Windows devices managed via Splashtop, transitioning from Pulseway) to Google Workspace within a 10-week window. Active Directory will be decommissioned, the ~10 SSO-integrated applications will be redirected to Google as the Identity Provider, and Microsoft Outlook mail and calendar will be migrated to Gmail and Google Calendar.

key_focus_areas.label: Mail & File Migration
key_focus_areas.text: CloudM Migrate-driven migration of mailboxes, OneDrive, and SharePoint using a dual-track wave approach with delta sync at cutover

key_focus_areas.label: Endpoint Identity Migration
key_focus_areas.text: Active Directory decommission via Google Credential Provider for Windows (GCPW) for Windows endpoints, with user data preserved on-device

key_focus_areas.label: SSO Re-pointing
key_focus_areas.text: Re-configuration of identified SSO-integrated applications to use Google as the Identity Provider, with per-application validation

key_focus_areas.label: Cutover & Decommission
key_focus_areas.text: MX, Autodiscover, SPF, DKIM DNS changes; Gmail and Calendar activation; Active Directory decommission and operational handover

background.engagement_type: This is an execution engagement. Premier Cloud will perform the migration end-to-end, including discovery, configuration, pilot, wave bulk migration, delta migration, cutover, and post-migration validation. Deliverables include a migrated Google Workspace tenant, CloudM reconciliation and validation reports, an AD decommission checklist, and final sign-off.

migration.destination_platform: Google Workspace (Gmail, Drive, Shared Drives, Calendar)

volumes.label: SharePoint
volumes.notes: includes OldEmployeeFiles (1.18 TB) and BrandUSAProduction (901 GB)

migration.plan_note: The Gantt chart provides a comprehensive 10-week roadmap for the Office 365 to Google Workspace migration, outlining key workstreams for data migration and endpoint identity configuration. It ensures all stakeholders have visibility into specific milestones, such as 'Pilot acceptance' and 'Cutover complete', and references the essential resources and infrastructure required for a successful transition.
decisions_pending: Miles Partnership IT completes the user mapping spreadsheet (source O365 user → target Google Workspace user) for all in-scope users and SharePoint sites by end of Week 1

Customer decisions on PST files (144 GB), OldEmployeeFiles SharePoint (1.18 TB), BrandUSAProduction SharePoint (901 GB), external sharing strategy (179K externally-shared items), and service-account handling are finalized before the Week 2 pilot

phases.name: Phase 1: Preparation & Discovery (Week 1)
activities: Pre-migration scan of the Microsoft 365 source tenant covering mailbox count and size distribution, OneDrive volume and file-type breakdown, SharePoint site inventory, externally-shared content, service/shared accounts, and PST/VMDK files
User mapping spreadsheet completed by Miles Partnership IT: source O365 user → target Google Workspace user for all in-scope accounts and SharePoint sites
Customer decisions documented for PST files, SharePoint retention, external sharing strategy (approximately 179,000 externally-shared items), and service-account handling

phases.name: Phase 2: Configuration & Readiness Scan (Week 1)
activities: CloudM Migrate instance provisioned in Google Cloud with 12 worker nodes (5 mail + 7 file)
Domain mappings configured per migration project; per-entity migration batches (mail, OneDrive, SharePoint, contacts, calendar) configured separately
CloudM readiness scan executed against the configured project to validate source/destination connectivity and surface configuration issues prior to pilot
Service-account and admin credentials provisioned in both tenants per CloudM prerequisites

phases.name: Phase 3: Pilot Migration (Week 2)
activities: Pilot group of 25 users selected across departments and mailbox-size profiles
Pilot covers mail and OneDrive migration with full data fidelity validation
Pilot acceptance criteria reviewed with Miles Partnership before proceeding to bulk waves

phases.name: Phase 4: Bulk Historical Migration in Waves (Weeks 3–9)
phases.intro: Migration is sequenced by mailbox size, smallest first, to maximize early CloudM worker utilization and contain risk:
activities: Wave 1 (Weeks 3–4): 316 mailboxes under 1 GB
Wave 2 (Weeks 5–6): 210 mailboxes 1–20 GB plus smaller SharePoint sites
Wave 3 (Weeks 7–8): 160 mailboxes 20–50 GB plus larger SharePoint sites
Wave 4 (Week 9): 20 mailboxes over 50 GB — delta pass only; pre-staging of bulk historical data for these mailboxes runs in the background from Week 3 onward

phases.name: Phase 5: Delta Migration & Cutover (Week 10)
activities: Final delta pass to capture new and changed mail and files since the last bulk pass
DNS cutover: MX, Autodiscover, SPF, DKIM, and any CNAMEs required for Google Workspace mail flow
Gmail and Google Calendar activated for all in-scope users
Microsoft 365 access frozen for in-scope users at the cutover boundary

phases.name: Phase 6: Post-Migration Validation (Week 10)
activities: CloudM reconciliation report reviewed for each migration batch
Spot-check audit of mailboxes and Drive folders against source counts
Known non-migrating items documented for user self-service: personal signatures, canned responses, and inbox filters/rules
Outstanding remediation items tracked to closure

tracks.name: Track B — Endpoint Identity Migration (AD → Google Login)
tracks.description: Track B runs in parallel with Track A. Endpoints are migrated in waves aligned to the data-migration waves.

phases.name: Phase 1: Endpoint Inventory & SSO Audit (Week 1)
activities: Inventory of all approximately 225 domain-joined Windows endpoints managed via Splashtop
Audit of the approximately 10 SSO-integrated applications currently authenticating via AD/Microsoft (ADP, Zoom, LastPass, and similar)
SSO re-pointing plan with per-application validation criteria

phases.name: Phase 2: Endpoint Pilot (Week 2)
activities: 10-device pilot covering Windows only

Windows flow validated: Splashtop-pushed scripts create local accounts (Local Admin and Local User), ForensIT Profwiz migrates the AD profile to the local user profile, domain unjoin is executed, and Google Credential Provider for Windows (GCPW) is installed
Active Directory kept live in parallel for two weeks post-pilot to enable rollback if needed

phases.name: Phase 3: Endpoint Migration Waves (Weeks 3–8)
activities: Wave A (Weeks 3–4): 45 Windows endpoints
Wave B (Weeks 5–6): 70 Windows endpoints
Wave C (Weeks 7–8): 65 Windows endpoints
VIP and executive endpoints are intentionally scheduled in the final wave

phases.name: Phase 4: Final Endpoint Wave & AD Decommission (Weeks 9–10)
activities: Final approximately 100 endpoints, including VIP machines
SSO applications re-pointed to Google as Identity Provider; each application validated against the test plan defined in Phase 1
Active Directory infrastructure decommissioned
Operational handover and decommission sign-off

scope.statement: This engagement is delivered in two parallel tracks executed over 10 weeks: Track A — Data Migration (mail, OneDrive, SharePoint), and Track B — Endpoint Identity Migration (Active Directory decommission, GCPW, Google SSO). Track A follows CloudM Migrate's documented methodology, applied in waves keyed to mailbox size distribution.
out_of_scope_extra: Migration of Microsoft Teams content — Slack is Miles Partnership's instant-messaging platform; a small Teams subset is retained out of scope

Video files are migrated by default. Users who wish to exclude video files must indicate this via the pre-migration opt-out tracking sheet. Opt-out users will be placed in a dedicated migration batch with video MIME types excluded at the batch level. Files exceeding 5 GB cannot be migrated, regardless of opt-out preference

assumptions: Splashtop MDM platform is operational throughout the migration window for pushing endpoint scripts and configuration profiles to Windows devices
Active Directory remains operational in parallel for the two weeks following the endpoint pilot to enable rollback
Network bandwidth from Microsoft 365 to the CloudM Migrate worker pool in Google Cloud is sufficient for the 24.8 TB total data volume; CloudM worker count and concurrency may be tuned during pilot
success_criteria: 100% of in-scope mailboxes migrated to Google Workspace with delta sync validated against the CloudM reconciliation report
100% of in-scope OneDrive and SharePoint content migrated to Google Drive and Shared Drives
100% of in-scope Windows endpoints (approximately 225 devices) transitioned to Google login via GCPW with user data preserved
Active Directory decommissioned and all SSO-integrated applications re-pointed to Google as Identity Provider, each application validated
Mail flow cutover (MX, SPF, DKIM, Autodiscover) completed with no inbound mail loss
Final cutover and decommission completed within the 10-week window
Final reports reviewed and validated by Miles Partnership stakeholders
